blogs.title: Procedural Rights in Vacuo: D.C. Circuit Reaffirms *Summers* Standing Requirements in FOIA Context
blogs.description: This post analyzes Judge Katsas's application of *Summers v. Earth Island Inst.* in the October 2025 decision *America First Legal Foundation v. Greer*. It examines why the court rejected the plaintiff's claim that a statutory right to an OSC investigation constitutes a concrete injury in itself, emphasizing the continuing requirement for a concrete interest beyond the procedural right.

blogs.title: The 'Independent Actor' Barrier: Causation Challenges in Multi-Agency Enforcement Schemes
blogs.description: Focusing on the causation element of standing, this post dissects the court's reliance on *FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine*. It explores how the speculative chain involving the OSC, MSPB, and DOJ broke the causal link, illustrating the high bar plaintiffs face when seeking to compel agency action through intermediate enforcement mechanisms.

blogs.title: FOIA Enforcement Limbo: The Unresolved Conflict Between OSC Authority and FOIA Statutes
blogs.description: While the D.C. Circuit dismissed the case on standing, this post explores the statutory tension left undecided between 5 U.S.C. § 1216 and FOIA § 552(a)(4)(F)(i). It discusses the implications of this avoidance for future litigation regarding whether the Office of Special Counsel has a mandatory duty to investigate arbitrary FOIA withholdings.
